body.x: On December 12th, AVING News orchestrated a networking event, connecting South Korean companies honored with the CES 2024 Innovation Awards with domestic and international media. This platform allowed AVING News to showcase the innovative technologies of Korean CES participants to the world.

During the event, figures from various media outlets like Ubergizmo, a US tech media outlet represented by Editor-in-Chief Hubert Nguyen, and Le Café du Geek from France, represented by Editor Leo Thevenet, joined Korean media sources such as IT DongA, I Love PC(SmartPC Sarang), and CNET Korea.
CES 2024 Innovation Award-winning companies DABIDA, BarunBio, and SAFEWARE presented their respective technological prowess and products at the event.

The CES Innovation Award, established in 1976 by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), honors innovative products and technologies showcasing technical, aesthetic, and creative aspects, receiving substantial credibility from industry experts.

body.cap: Lee Eun-seung, CEO of DABIDA, presented DABIDA’s products and services. │ Photo by AVING News

body.x: Edutech startup DABIDA, led by CEO Lee Eun-seung, clinched the CES 2024 Innovation Award in the Smart City category for their core technology—a live video platform called ‘GeniClass.’ This platform synchronizes various ICT devices in real-time, notably introducing innovation in remote learning through user-friendly interfaces like ‘GeniPen,’ a digital-analog hybrid product. It allows real-time confirmation and digital text conversion of handwritten notes from GeniPen to the GeniClass platform, facilitating instant teacher feedback.

Additionally, utilizing data from the pen regarding time, strokes, etc., DABIDA offers a data-centric, efficient approach to enhance individual academic performance by analyzing students’ learning tendencies, problem-solving time, attention span, and cognitive actions, including errors.

BarunBio, represented by CEO Hong Jin-ki, secured the CES 2024 Innovation Award in the Wearable Technology category for their ‘WE-STIM (Wearable Electric Stimulation) Leggings.’ These leggings harness micro-electric energy generated from everyday movements without needing batteries or devices, marking a unique anti-aging technology developed over a decade.

The awarded WE-STIM leggings, beyond being mere fashion items, utilize energy derived from human routine movements for health and wellness. The WE-STIM material within the leggings continuously generates micro-electric energy based on human motion, transmitting it to the muscles effectively. BarunBio’s technology employs structural engineering and conductive fibers to implement the WE-STIM structure within traditional clothing materials, aiming to efficiently deliver harvested energy to the body.

body.cap: Song Hyun-hee, General Manager of BarunBio, explained BarunBio’s solutions. │ Photo by AVING News
Jang Sung-hwan, General Manager of Safeware, explained Safeware’s products. │ Photo by AVING News

body.x: SafeWare, a human safety solution company led by CEO Shin Hwan-chul, garnered the CES 2024 Innovation Award in the Human Safety Product category for their ‘Personal Mobility Airbag Vest.’ This wearable airbag, designed for users of personal mobility devices like electric scooters, wheels, and bicycles, safeguards vulnerable body parts upon detecting user accidents using motion-sensing sensors within the wearable airbag. The integrated product sensor can function for over 100 hours upon complete charging and allows cartridge module replacement for reuse even after the airbag deployment.

Previously, SafeWare received acclaim for its technology and innovation through CES 2022 and 2023 Innovation Awards for its Elderly Fall Protection Airbag Belt and Smart Fall Protection Airbag C3. The latter has successfully commercialized, supplying over 10,000 units to approximately 660 domestic companies and institutions like Samsung, LG, POSCO E&C, Korea Expressway Corporation, and KEPCO.

body.cap: Four companies presented their physical products during the event. (From upper left, clockwise) The Whot Brewery with its craft beers, Levitate with its EBLE Highballs, RETEM with its ice maker, and LIDART with its CMYK UP lighting. │ Photo by AVING News

body.x: Moreover, the event held at U2 Lounge in Seoul’s Seocho-gu introduced different avenues for sensory satisfaction, featuring The Whot Brewery, a craft beer company using Gyeonggi Icheon rice, Levitate, a producer of its highball brand EBLE, RETEM, an ice maker manufacturer, and LIDART, making lighting products enhancing artistic aspects of spaces.
The event concluded with the ‘Lucky Draw Event,’ receiving significant participation. The prizes for the draw were items prepared by the attendees, adding to the event’s excitement.

Kim Kidai, Publisher of AVING News, expressed during his address, “AVING News is on the verge of completing its headquarters. This space will be utilized as a membership space for startups. I hope to share the positive energy of this space and grow together for a mutually prosperous 2024.”

body.cap: Kim Kidai, Publisher of AVING News, delivering a speech. │Photo by AVING News

body.x: The Consumer Technology Association (CTA) organizes CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition, in Las Vegas every January. AVING News, reporting on CES for 18 consecutive years since 2006, has conducted ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA,’ selecting the finest innovative products, companies, and technologies. Additionally, they’ve conveyed live CES updates through ‘AVING LIVE.’
